title: Reverse-Engineering a macOS Driver for the Orphaned Drobo 5D Using AI Assistance
summary: The author documents their process of using an AI assistant (Claude) to reverse-engineer and develop a macOS driver for the Drobo 5D, a discontinued RAID array, to maintain compatibility with future macOS versions. The project involved analyzing the existing Drobo Dashboard software, decoding the proprietary ESA management protocol, and building a functional driver and CLI/GUI replacement without official support or documentation.
key_points: Drobo 5D, a discontinued RAID array, faces compatibility issues with newer macOS versions due to the lack of updated drivers and Rosetta 2 deprecation.
The author used Claude (an AI assistant) to analyze the Drobo Dashboard software and firmware, identifying why it fails on newer macOS versions.
The project followed a 5-phase plan: data protection, protocol validation, payload decoding, CLI development, and a full driver replacement.
Key challenges included macOS's lack of SCSITaskUserClient support for the Drobo, requiring reverse-engineering of the ESA protocol via a working iMac setup.
The author disabled System Integrity Protection (SIP) on a spare MacMini to test the AI-generated driver, encountering multiple entitlement and compilation issues.

After troubleshooting, the driver successfully read device information (e.g., array health, drive serials) and was packaged into a GUI app (ReDrobo) with features like notifications and diagnostics export.
The project highlights the potential of AI-assisted coding for niche hardware support but notes the lack of deep learning due to the hands-off approach.
Source code and documentation are available on GitHub (fetzu/ReDrobo) for others to extend the Drobo's lifespan, though it requires disabling SIP.
